my_own_additional_files.reading: TWO conclusions. (i) My detection path is live: run against declarations that do contain sorry, this exact command prints sorryAx. The NO in every other run is therefore a measurement, not a blind spot. (ii) See naming_hazard below - this is NOT a RED.

naming_hazard_I_FOUND.what: ComparatorChallenges/NavierStokes.lean opens namespace NavierStokes.Comparator and declares theorems named navier_stokes_breakdown_R3 (line 273) and navier_stokes_breakdown_periodic (line 280), both proved by sorry. Their FULLY-QUALIFIED NAMES are character-for-character the two names K1 checked. The same holds on the Euler side: ComparatorChallenges/Euler.lean declares Euler.euler_breakdown_R3 and Euler.exists_compact_smooth_euler_singularity by sorry - the same two names Euler/Solution.lean exports.
naming_hazard_I_FOUND.consequence: #print axioms NavierStokes.Comparator.navier_stokes_breakdown_R3 returns the standard three axioms, or the standard three PLUS sorryAx, depending purely on which module the checking file imports. The name does not determine the answer.
naming_hazard_I_FOUND.is_this_a_RED: NO, and the reason must be stated precisely. The exported theorem is defined by ComparatorChallenges/NavierStokes.json: solution_module = NavierStokes.ComparatorSolution, theorem_names = the two names, permitted_axioms = [propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice]. The runner's check file imports exactly that solution_module, and I measured that the names resolve there to declarations in NavierStokes.ComparatorSolution, whose import closure contains neither challenge module. sorryAx is reachable only from the reference placeholders in the challenge modules, which nothing imports. The prereg's RED condition - sorryAx reachable from an exported theorem - is NOT met.
naming_hazard_I_FOUND.but: this IS the failure mode worth recording. The K1 artefacts assert an axiom list against a bare name, and the bare name is ambiguous inside this very repository. What makes K1's answer the right one is the import line, not the name. Anyone re-running #print axioms on these names from a different environment - for instance while auditing the challenge files - will get sorryAx, and should not read it as a contradiction of K1.

part_b.what_my_part_b_run_does_and_does_not_add: It adds: a second agent, executing the runner's own unmodified file, reaching byte-identical output, plus three checks the runner never ran (module provenance, all four theorems, a live sorryAx control). It does not add a rebuild. The oleans I queried were compiled by the k2 support rebuild on this laptop earlier today; #print axioms reads a compiled environment, it does not re-run the kernel over the proof terms. My run confirms the recorded axiom result at this pin; it does not independently re-elaborate the proofs.
